findings_and_qualified_observations.classification: Newly assessed current source candidate, conditional public API contract; central owner determines aliases and whether counted.
findings_and_qualified_observations.trace: The generic Transform publicly represents per-axis scale and has a constructor taking it without a positivity check. from_mat4 extracts each column length and divides components by those scales; for the finite affine diagonal matrix diag(1,1,0,1), scale.z is zero and r22 is 0/0, so the returned X rotation becomes NaN via atan2. A zero-axis scale is representable through the generic API. The separate public JointTransform::to_transform conversion calls this same from_mat4, while the shown auto-rigger conversion builds translation-only matrices and does not establish a collapsed input.
findings_and_qualified_observations.condition: The diagonal case is symbolic source reasoning, not a fabricated or executed product fixture. No actual caller, imported asset, enabled product path, accepted zero scale, or rendered/retained bad animation value observed. Whether a collapsed scale should be a supported transform, rejected input, or an explicit no-unique-rotation case is unresolved.
findings_and_qualified_observations.historical_relationship: 059 READ-L11-450 explicitly left from_mat4 as uninspected connected callee; 774 Rig role2751 excluded111–322. q171 ADLER-L11-MHR-BIND-TRANSFORM-ADMISSION is related singularity policy in the distinct f64 MHR bind owner, not an automatic alias. findings_and_qualified_observations.future_repair_direction: Decide the zero/degenerate-scale contract at the shared transform decomposition boundary and either return a meaningful rejection or provide a defined representation for the supported collapsed case; coordinate the JointTransform conversion while preserving valid Euler ordering, per-axis scales and intentional raw matrix boundaries.

findings_and_qualified_observations.classification: Newly assessed current source candidate from a previously open 059 look_at policy, conditional on supported inputs; central reconciliation decides count.
findings_and_qualified_observations.trace: For eye=(1,0,0), target=(1,0,1), up=(0,0,0.1), the forward and up directions are parallel. Their cross product is zero; the branch picks alternate up=(0,0,1) because up.z is below 0.9, which is also parallel to forward. Normalizing zero leaves it zero. The constructed view is singular; inverse returns None, Transform::look_at replaces it with the identity matrix and decomposition therefore returns zero position rather than the nonzero eye.
findings_and_qualified_observations.condition: The example is mathematical source reasoning only. Up-vector magnitude is not explicitly constrained in these displayed APIs, but the intended degenerate look direction/up policy and supported external consumers are unknown. Exact-spelling 95e search found the method itself and a source-only test, no identified non-test direct first-party call; aliases, method references and external consumers remain open. No rendered failure or runtime behavior observed.
findings_and_qualified_observations.historical_relationship: 059 Segovb READ-L11-450 noted default inverse and explicitly left its native context unclosed. This is new bounded analysis, not an assumed duplicate or historical accepted finding.
findings_and_qualified_observations.future_repair_direction: Specify failure or fallback semantics for degenerate look inputs; if fallback is supported, select a stable alternate axis based on forward direction and preserve the requested eye, with typed failure where a direction cannot be established.
